previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, chronic pain, and recent steroid use was admitted with acute left lower quadrant abdominal pain and watery diarrhea following a meal with a friend who also became ill. Initial concern for a Crohn’s flare was ruled out by normal inflammatory markers and stable findings on recent imaging. Stool studies showed no bacterial, parasitic, or C. difficile infection, supporting a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis. The patient was managed supportively with IV then oral pain control. Azathioprine was held due to mild thrombocytopenia. Pain Management recommended starting tizanidine and Lyrica for chronic pain. The patient improved clinically and was discharged home on prednisone, pantoprazole, loperamide as needed, and new pain medications, with instructions to follow up with gastroenterology and pain specialists.
problems: Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified

Brief Hospital Course:
___ old male with longstanding ___ disease s/p partial 
colectomy/ileosigmoidostomy, chronic abd pain was admitted once 
again with worsening/severe diarrhea and n/v c/w prior ___ 
flare. This time triggered by bad meal day prior. WAs also 
significantly volume depleted with acidosis and ARF on 
admission. While abdominal pain was worse than baseline, it was 
still consistent with prior flares where repeated imaging had 
not revealed any abscess/perf. GI saw pt and defered repeat 
imaging with plans to treat conservatively. His stool cx were 
negative, including O&P. He as managed with bowel rest, 
aggressive fluids (with improvement in renal function to 
baseline 2.0->1.2), pain meds, cipro (10day course), increased 
prednisone (15mg->40mg). He improved over two days and was able 
to slowly advance diet over next two days.  His leukocytosis 
also resolved with this management. Plan is to taper pred slowly 
by 5mg/week until he is back on his usual dose of 15mg (doesnt 
tolerate less than this). he will finish 10day cipro course. He 
is followed by pain clinic and was not discharged on narcotics 
which he recieved while here. He is on chronic pred but cant 
affort Ca/Vit D though is encouraged to take this. He has h/o 
Vit B12 def (level repeat 711), for which he cant afford daily 
supp, so we gave him a 1000mcg shot here (gets monthly as 
outpt). He is kept on his lyrica and xanaflex for his LUQ pain-
